Pet owners warned after cat is mutilated and killed by sick human with knife on Milton Keynes estate

By Sally Murrer
Published 30th Sep 2026, 13:36 BST
Updated 30th Sep 2026, 14:02 BST

A devastated family has issued a warning to all cat owners after their pet was found horrifically mutilated and killed by a knife-carrying human.

0:00 / 3:17

Much-loved tortoiseshell cat Bella went missing on Sunday (September 27) from her house on Whitehouse estate.

Her owners were puzzled as she was never a cat that strayed far from home. They’d had her for 10 years, since she was a kitten, and she followed them everywhere and always came running when they called her name.

They searched the estate to no avail and put on a post on the Whitehouse Facebook Page asking if anyone had seen her.

"A lady walking her dog immediately alerted us that sadly she was deceased in the field next to Watling Academy school. The same field we had searched and the same field she always hung out in... the same field that my child walks to and from school through,” said the owner.

She added: “I found Bella where the lady told me and it utterly sickens me to the core to say that she had been mutilated. Her tail had been clean cut off right at the base and was nowhere to be seen.”

The vet later confirmed the tail had been cut off deliberately with a blade. Bella’s neck had also been broken and ever her legs were twisted out of shape.

The family believe the evil offender had picked up Bella from near their home, killed her, then dumped her in the field.

"To say my legs went from under me when I saw her wouldn’t even describe it. ” said the owner. “How can anyone do this to a defenceless animal and murder it? It is absolutely sick.”

Worryingly, it is feared Bella may not be the only victim of the MK mutilator.

"Sadly, the vets has said it is not uncommon and seems to happen in spates,” said the owner. "After I posted about Bella, I had a call from a local vets to say they’d had two other cats brought in recently with their tails cut off….There is an evil person out there.”

Bella’s family are struggling to come to terms with their loss but have bravely posted her story on social media to warn other people that a cat mutilator is on the loose.

“If it saves other cats, it needs to be written,” they said. “Please if you have a cat in Milton Keynes, please think twice about letting them out.

“We as a family are utterly devastated and will not get the image out of our heads. RIP Bella, I am so so sorry that you were subjected to such evil.”

Meanwhile, the owner has reported the matter to police, who have replied giving a crime reference number for “criminal damage”.

"We also reported it to the RSPCA and they are taking it seriously and coming out to visit the area,” she said.

In the UK, cutting off a cat's tail is classified as an illegal mutilation and causing unnecessary suffering under the Animal Welfare Act 2006. Under the Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021, the maximum prison sentence is five years and/or an unlimited fine.
